zone.title: Assumed planting zone
zone.text: This rectangle is an example of the area you want to plant, not a map of your parcel. Drag an edge to change its shape while keeping the same area.
zone.caution: Plants left outside the rectangle stay on your list as unplaced.

approaches.title: Approaches and plant combinations
approaches.text: MR1 illustrates mixed planting on degraded land. MR2 illustrates planting islands that collect rainfall. You can combine them and edit the suggested plants.
approaches.caution: These examples do not check whether a plant will thrive on your land.

combinations.title: Vegetation combinations
combinations.text: A combination suggests plants found together or used in an example mix. Shared species appear once, and your edited densities and prices are kept.
combinations.caution: A vegetation series describes a plant community, not a ready-made planting recipe.

dimensions.title: Plant dimensions
dimensions.text: The dashed circle shows an estimated mature crown or plant spread. The small solid circle shows the root ball at planting; it is a separate drawing size.
dimensions.caution: These circles do not predict growth or the underground root system. Overlapping crowns are allowed.

placement.title: Placing plants
placement.text: New plants are positioned automatically. Drag them, or focus a plant symbol and use arrow keys; Shift moves further and Escape cancels. Moving a tree also moves shrubs still linked to it; moving a shrub separately breaks that link.
placement.caution: Plant combinations and positions are planning examples, not proof of suitable growing conditions.

mulch.title: Surface mulch
mulch.text: A mulch ring marks a surface treatment around the chosen plants. Choose the material and edit its radius.
mulch.caution: The drawing does not calculate material, labour, watering savings or treatment costs.

unplaced.title: Unplaced plants
unplaced.text: These plants are on your purchasing list, but have no position inside the zone. Use Place next in zone, then drag the selected plant or move it with arrow keys.
unplaced.caution: Their quantities and costs are still included.

density.title: Density and spacing
density.text: Density means plants per hectare: 10,000 m². It is calculated over the entire planting zone. Literature gives different densities, so the app uses adjustable starting values rather than one established target.
density.example: Seven trees on 200 m² equal 350 trees/ha, whether grouped closely together or spread across the zone. Spacing is the distance between individual plants.

pocket.title: Assumed moisture pocket
pocket.text: A moisture pocket marks a spot you expect to stay moister. One moisture pocket is supported.
pocket.caution: The app does not measure soil moisture. Drawing a larger pocket does not establish that enough water is available.

states.off: The moisture pocket is switched off.
states.linked: Dragging it also moves the example encina, unless you move the tree separately.
states.independent: You moved the example encina separately, so it no longer follows the pocket.
states.unplaced: The example encina is on the plant list but is unplaced. Place it in the zone to see its crown.
states.absent: No example encina is currently on the planting list.

pocket.crown: The dashed circle shows the example tree’s crown, not a second moisture pocket.
pocket.crown_hidden: Crown display is off. Switch on Indicative mature crowns to see the tree’s circle.
pocket.extra: Additional encinas come from the plant-density setting; they do not mark additional moisture pockets.

mr1.title: MR1 · Recover degraded land
mr1.text: Start with mixed plants in small groups and leave some ground open. Prefer places with better soil or moisture where these are known.
mr1.caution: The drawn groups do not identify real favourable spots on your land.

mr2.title: MR2 · Collect rainfall
mr2.text: Planting islands receive runoff from nearby open ground. Arrows show the idea of water flowing towards them and leaving through an overflow.
mr2.caution: This is a sketch, not a drainage design. Check slopes, erosion and safe overflow on site.

stone_mulch.title: Stone mulch
stone_mulch.text: Stone around a plant is one traditional surface treatment used in dryland planting.
stone_mulch.caution: Keep the root collar clear. The ring size is an editable drawing assumption, not a tested prescription.

autumn.title: Planting season and young carob plants

sections.title: When to plant
paragraphs: For carob, aim for autumn or early winter once the soil has suitable moisture. A broader November–March window appears in the handbook, but local frost risk and soil conditions matter more than the calendar alone.

Planting early gives roots time to establish before the first dry summer. Delays can be especially risky on shallow or very stony soils, where little water is stored. Avoid planting into dry, frozen or waterlogged ground.
Arrange nursery delivery close to the planting date. Keep plants sheltered and root balls moist until planting; protect them from sun, drying wind and damage during transport.

sections.title: Choosing young plants
paragraphs: Nursery stock means young plants raised for planting out. Una savia means one growing season; it does not by itself guarantee good roots or a sturdy plant.

For this restoration example, ask for seed-grown, ungrafted carob with a recorded seed origin. Check for healthy, branching roots without tight coils, an intact root ball that holds together, and a healthy balance between shoots and roots.

Ask whether plants have been hardened: gradually accustomed to outdoor sun, wind and drier conditions before leaving the nursery. Protect the shoots and root ball in transport, and avoid leaving plants exposed while waiting to plant.

The references describe 0.2–0.3 L forestry containers and 1–2 L alternatives. A 1 L plant is a candidate for this pilot, supported by the nursery discussion and nearby Níjar purchasing example; it is not a proven optimum. Root quality, seed origin and hardening matter alongside container volume.

survival.title: Survival is uncertain
survival.text: Historical Almería examples report 40–60% carob survival. That observation is not a forecast for this design.
survival.caution: The cited passage does not establish a monitoring period or a survival rate for your site.

care.title: Establishment care
care.text: Plan planting dates, protection and checks through the first dry seasons. Watering needs depend on soil, rainfall, plant quality and care.
care.caution: The app does not calculate a watering schedule or guarantee survival. See the carob guide for the reported field examples.

root_ball_default.title: Root balls at planting
root_ball_default.text: The root-ball circle uses the design’s saved drawing size unless you enter a measured size.
root_ball_default.caution: It is illustrative. Container litres do not establish a root-ball diameter or a planting-hole size.

treeless_series.title: Shrub series without trees
treeless_series.text: New shrubs from the lentisco and coscoja series can stand alone when no planned trees are drawn. With trees present, the usual crown-placement preference applies. Your placement choices take priority.
treeless_series.caution: Existing plants keep their positions. This is an example layout, not a suitability assessment.

combinations.mr1_mix: Algarrobo starts this mixed restoration example. Alcornoque is a less frequent associate in the handbook, absent from poster system 3. The book says labiérnago without distinguishing both Phillyrea species; offering both is our interpretation. Choose companions for the actual site.
combinations.mr2_mix: A starter selection for planting islands and rainfall capture, not a calculated water requirement.
combinations.lentisk_series: A reference community centred on lentisco, with an illustrative subset of companions rather than a complete planting recipe. The source heading and scientific name disagree; see Sources and details.
combinations.coscoja_series: Coscoja and espino negro represent the named reference community. Optional ephedra, retama and esparto illustrate related vegetation or stages, not a compulsory mixture.
combinations.system_woodland: An illustrative woodland-and-shrub mix. It does not establish that every suggested species suits your site.
combinations.system_scrub: An illustrative Mediterranean scrub mix, with editable plants and densities.
combinations.system_arid: An illustrative selection for exploring dry, open vegetation; actual water and soil conditions still need checking.
combinations.system_watercourse: An illustrative selection associated with watercourses. Selecting it does not establish that water is available.

placement.associated: Placed within {parent}’s estimated crown. It moves with that tree until you move this plant separately.
placement.manual: You positioned this plant. It stays here when other trees move.
placement.tree: An example tree position. Drag it to adjust the layout.
placement.open_ground: Initially placed outside the drawn tree crowns. You can move it.
placement.independent: An example position in the planting zone. You can move it.

unplaced.with_tree_outside: Moved outside the zone with its tree.
unplaced.outside: Its saved position is outside the current zone.
unplaced.no_tree: No planned tree crown is available. Place this plant manually or change its automatic placement preference for future additions.
unplaced.not_positioned: No position has been assigned inside the zone. There may not be enough space with the current placement settings.
